confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer anchors on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living data: Expatica's summary of Numbeo data from June 2026 (inexpensive meal about $20, three-course meal for two about $85, draught beer about $6, cappuccino about $4.97) and MyLifeElsewhere (inexpensive meal with a drink about $24.50, pint of beer about $6, cappuccino about $4.93). I raised these slightly to allow for tourist-area pricing and price growth by July 2026. Cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. They are a bounded estimate from mixed sources: Expatistan's crowd-sourced guess of about $15 for a cocktail, which used only 7 data points; happy-hour deals of $9-10 listed by Visit Orlando; and the usual US ratio of drink prices to beer. Accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge. I did not check live booking pages or listings. Orlando has very few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are the least certain. July is a busy family-travel season for the theme parks, so the hotel anchors reflect moderately elevated summer rates for the International Drive and Kissimmee areas.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink prices are in line with large tourism-driven cities in the US Sun Belt, such as Tampa and Las Vegas off the Strip. Survey data shows Orlando restaurant prices slightly below Chicago and Los Angeles. Accommodation is based on Orlando's large supply of budget motels and mid-range chain hotels around International Drive and Kissimmee, plus a very small hostel market.
